convert_gregorian_to_hijri.description: Turn a Gregorian date into its Hijri one, with the day of the week in English and Arabic and any holiday that falls on it. Leave the date empty for today, so a scheduled workflow can post the Hijri date each morning with nothing filled in.

options.label: South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands

parameters.description: Fill in one of three ways to name the place: a city and its country, an address, or a latitude and longitude. Latitude in decimal degrees, from -90 to 90. Coordinates are the exact way to name a place, and the only one that reports the position back unmasked.

parameters.description: Which authority's angles to compute the times with. Leave empty and AlAdhan uses the authority closest to the place, which is right far more often than a guess. Run 'List calculation methods' to see the angles each one sets.

options.label: Institute of Geophysics, University of Tehran
Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Russia
Ministry of Awqaf, Islamic Affairs and Holy Places, Jordan

parameters.description: Which juristic method places Asr. The Hanafi position puts it later in the afternoon than the other three schools. Defaults to the majority position.

options.label: Shafi, Maliki and Hanbali (the majority position)

parameters.description: Where midnight falls: halfway from sunset to sunrise, or halfway from sunset to Fajr. Defaults to the first.

options.label: Standard: halfway from sunset to sunrise

parameters.description: What to do where the sun never drops far enough below the horizon for Fajr and Isha to have a true time, which is most of northern Europe in summer. Only worth setting above roughly 48 degrees of latitude.

parameters.description: Fill in one of three ways to name the place: a city and its country, an address, or a latitude and longitude. Latitude in decimal degrees, from -90 to 90. Coordinates are the exact way to name a place, and the only one that reports the position back unmasked.
parameters.name: latitude

parameters.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, from -180 to 180. The Americas take a negative longitude.
parameters.name: longitude

parameters.description: Which authority's angles to compute the times with. Leave empty and AlAdhan uses the authority closest to the place, which is right far more often than a guess. Run 'List calculation methods' to see the angles each one sets.
parameters.name: method

options.label: Institute of Geophysics, University of Tehran
Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Russia
Ministry of Awqaf, Islamic Affairs and Holy Places, Jordan

parameters.description: Which juristic method places Asr. The Hanafi position puts it later in the afternoon than the other three schools. Defaults to the majority position.
parameters.name: school

options.label: Shafi, Maliki and Hanbali (the majority position)

parameters.description: Where midnight falls: halfway from sunset to sunrise, or halfway from sunset to Fajr. Defaults to the first.
parameters.name: midnight_mode

options.label: Standard: halfway from sunset to sunrise
Jafari: halfway from sunset to Fajr

parameters.description: What to do where the sun never drops far enough below the horizon for Fajr and Isha to have a true time, which is most of northern Europe in summer. Only worth setting above roughly 48 degrees of latitude.
parameters.name: high_latitude_rule

parameters.description: Which twilight places Isha. Applies only to the Moonsighting Committee Worldwide method, and is ignored with any other, so it is sent only when that method is chosen.
parameters.name: shafaq

parameters.description: The timezone to report the times in. Leave empty and AlAdhan works it out from the place, which is almost always what you want. It also decides what 'today' means when the date is left blank.
parameters.name: timezone

parameters.description: How a Gregorian date is turned into a Hijri one. Defaults to the High Judiciary Council of Saudi Arabia, which is what aladhan.com itself shows. Run 'List Hijri calendar methods' to see what each covers.
parameters.name: calendar_method

options.label: High Judiciary Council of Saudi Arabia (default)

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Imsak by, from -120 to 120. Imsak is the end of the pre-dawn meal. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_imsak

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Fajr by, from -120 to 120. A local mosque commonly runs a minute or two later. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_fajr

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Sunrise by, from -120 to 120. Sunrise ends the time for Fajr. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_sunrise

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Dhuhr by, from -120 to 120. Dhuhr is the midday prayer. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_dhuhr

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Asr by, from -120 to 120. Asr is the afternoon prayer. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_asr

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Maghrib by, from -120 to 120. Maghrib is the sunset prayer. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_maghrib

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Sunset by, from -120 to 120. Sunset is the marker Maghrib is measured from. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_sunset

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Isha by, from -120 to 120. Isha is the night prayer. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_isha

parameters.description: Minutes to shift Midnight by, from -120 to 120. Midnight marks the last third of the night. Leave empty for no adjustment.
parameters.name: tune_midnight

get_qibla_compass.description: Get a compass picture marking the Qibla from a set of coordinates, as an image address to put in a message or a page. The picture is checked and described rather than downloaded, so the step returns a link rather than a hundred and fifty kilobytes of image.
get_qibla_compass.name: get_qibla_compass

parameters.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, from -90 to 90.
parameters.name: latitude

parameters.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, from -180 to 180. The Americas take a negative longitude.
parameters.name: longitude

get_qibla_direction.description: Get the compass bearing from a set of coordinates to the Kaaba in Makkah. The answer carries the exact bearing, a rounded one, and the compass point it corresponds to, plus the address of a compass picture showing it.
get_qibla_direction.name: get_qibla_direction

parameters.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, from -90 to 90.
parameters.name: latitude

parameters.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, from -180 to 180. The Americas take a negative longitude.
parameters.name: longitude

get_ramadan_islamic_year.description: Find which Hijri year holds the Ramadan that falls in a given Gregorian year. A Hijri year is eleven days shorter than a Gregorian one, so the two drift: this is the lookup that turns 'Ramadan 2027' into the year number the calendar actions take.
get_ramadan_islamic_year.display_name: Get the Hijri year of a Gregorian year's Ramadan
get_ramadan_islamic_year.display_str_template: Get the Hijri year of Ramadan in {0}.
get_ramadan_islamic_year.name: get_ramadan_islamic_year

parameters.description: The Gregorian year Ramadan falls in. Leave empty for this year.
parameters.name: year

list_calculation_methods.description: List every prayer-times calculation method AlAdhan supports, with the Fajr and Isha angles each one sets and the place it is associated with. Run it once to see which authority a region follows before pinning a workflow to one.
list_calculation_methods.name: list_calculation_methods

list_calendar_methods.description: List the ways AlAdhan can turn a Gregorian date into a Hijri one, with what each is based on and the range of years it is tabulated for. Read it before changing the calendar method on any of the other actions.

methods.description: The Umm al-Qura calendar, adjusted after reported sightings.
methods.name: High Judiciary Council of Saudi Arabia
methods.validity: 1356 AH (14 March 1937 CE) to 1500 AH (16 November 2077 CE)

list_calendar_methods.name: list_calendar_methods

list_hijri_holidays_for_year.description: List every holiday of a Hijri year with the Gregorian date each one falls on. Use it to fill a calendar a year at a time. AlAdhan sends one entry per observance, so days that carry several are merged here and the count is a count of days.
list_hijri_holidays_for_year.name: list_hijri_holidays_for_year

parameters.description: The Hijri year, from 1356 AH to 1500 AH, which is the range AlAdhan's calendars are tabulated for. Run 'Get the current Islamic date' if you need to know which year it is now.
parameters.name: hijri_year

parameters.description: How a Gregorian date is turned into a Hijri one. Defaults to the High Judiciary Council of Saudi Arabia, which is what aladhan.com itself shows. Run 'List Hijri calendar methods' to see what each covers.
parameters.name: calendar_method

options.label: High Judiciary Council of Saudi Arabia (default)

parameters.description: Shift the converted Hijri date by whole days, from -5 to 5, for a local moon sighting that ran a day ahead or behind. AlAdhan applies it only under the Mathematical calendar method, so choose that method too.
parameters.name: adjustment

list_islamic_months.description: List the twelve months of the Hijri calendar with their names in English and Arabic and the number each one takes in the other actions here.
list_islamic_months.name: list_islamic_months

list_names_of_allah.description: List all ninety-nine names of Allah in Arabic, with their transliteration and their meaning in English. A search term narrows the list to the names whose transliteration or meaning contains it, which is matched here since the API takes no search of its own.
list_names_of_allah.name: list_names_of_allah

parameters.description: Optional. Keep only the names whose transliteration or meaning contains this text. Leave empty for all ninety-nine.
parameters.name: search

list_special_days.description: List every special day of the Hijri calendar by the day and month it sits on. This is the fixed list, the same whatever the year, so it is the reference to check a day against without asking for a particular year's calendar.
list_special_days.name: list_special_days

description: Islamic prayer times, the Hijri calendar and the Qibla, from the free AlAdhan API. Get a day's prayer times or the next prayer due for any city, address or set of coordinates, publish a month, a year or the whole of Ramadan as a timetable, convert dates between the Gregorian and Hijri calendars, look up Islamic holidays and special days, find the compass bearing to the Kaaba, and read the ninety-nine names of Allah. Twenty-three calculation methods are supported, along with the Hanafi Asr, high-latitude rules and per-prayer minute adjustments. No account or API key is required.
